form_analysis.feedback: Excellent, detailed, and cautious aftercare for a significant procedure. Provides a clear day-by-day guide, manages expectations for substantial peeling/swelling, and includes strong warnings about herpes simplex reactivation and hyperpigmentation risk. A model form for this depth of treatment.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare protocol is for a medium-depth peel (e.g., TCA 15-35%, modified Jessner's). This treatment creates a controlled injury to the mid-layers of skin. Strict adherence to these instructions is VITAL for safe healing, to minimise discomfort, and to prevent scarring or pigment changes.

instructions.general_directive: Follow the General Chemical Peel Principles WITHOUT DEVIATION. The instructions below are specific to your medium-depth peel.

sections.title: Expected Healing Timeline & Symptoms
sections.content: DAY 1-2: Significant redness, swelling, tightness. Skin may feel like a severe sunburn. DAY 2-4: Swelling peaks. Skin darkens (frosts), becomes taut, then begins to peel, often starting around the mouth. DAY 4-7: Intensive peeling phase. Pink, new skin is revealed underneath. DAY 7-10: Peeling completes. Skin is uniformly pink, smooth, and may be shiny. DAY 10-14+: Pinkness gradually fades. Meticulous sun care begins.

sections.title: Specific Post-Peel Care Protocol
items: Antiviral Medication: If prescribed, take it as directed to prevent a cold sore outbreak.
Cleansing/Frequent Soaks: You will likely be instructed to soak or gently cleanse the area 4-6 times per day with a specific solution (e.g., diluted vinegar) to prevent crusting and soothe the skin.
Moisturizing/Ointment: Apply the provided healing ointment (e.g., petroleum jelly, specialized cream) LIBERALLY and CONSTANTLY after each cleanse/soak. The skin should never feel dry or tight.
Cool Compresses: Use cool, soft compresses frequently in the first 48 hours to reduce swelling and burning sensation.
Elevation: Sleep on your back with your head elevated on 2-3 pillows for the first 3-4 nights.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions (Strict)
items: Absolutely NO exercise, sweating, or heat exposure until your practitioner confirms healing is complete (usually 7-10 days).
Plan for 3-5 days of social downtime. You will be visibly peeling.
Do not pick, scratch, or assist the peeling in any way.

sections.title: Sun Protection (Hypervigilant)
sections.content: Once the initial peeling phase is over (Day 7-10), you MUST begin using a gentle physical sunscreen (zinc oxide/titanium dioxide) every day. For the first 4-6 weeks, avoid direct sun exposure entirely. This is the most critical period for preventing post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH).

sections.title: Complication Awareness - Contact Us IMMEDIATELY for:
items: Yellow/green pus or increasing pain/swelling/redness (signs of infection).
Severe itching, hives, or a blistering rash (allergic reaction).
Any area that is not peeling but appears dark, purple, or grey (possible necrosis).

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: Do NOT apply any makeup until all peeling has finished and your practitioner gives the okay (typically Day 7-10).

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: Itching is very common during peeling. An oral antihistamine can help.
The new skin will be pink for several weeks and is very delicate.
Full results, including improvement in wrinkles, scars, and pigmentation, are assessed at 6-8 weeks post-peel. A series of 1-3 peels may be recommended.
Attend ALL scheduled follow-up appointments (often at 24-48 hours, 1 week, and 1 month).
